clue.text: Exercise requiring words of encouragement

definitions.meaning: a gym exercise lifting the body until the jaw clears a bar
a cheering phrase telling someone to keep their spirits high

explanation.surface: A workout that needs someone shouting support from the sidelines.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one spelling: a gym pull-up variant and a cheery phrase urging someone to stay brave.

clue.text: Fine leaves boss of kitchen covering a problem

indicators.note: covering says the shortened title wraps round the word a
leaves says the letter for fine departs from the kitchen boss's title

parts.note: the person in charge of a restaurant kitchen is the head chef
F is the pencil-grade and fines abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A senior cook walks out, leaving the kitchen with a problem to cover up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes F out of HEADCHEF to give HEADCHE; 'covering' then wraps that round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A headache in the figurative sense is any nagging difficulty or worry.

clue.text: Can he con criminal? Absolutely not!

indicators.note: criminal suggests these letters are crooked, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man could pull off a swindle, and gets an emphatic refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' shuffles CANHECON.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiomatic emphatic refusal, meaning there is no possibility at all.

clue.text: Minister's responsibility for output of artist

definitions.meaning: a government minister's area of responsibility, as in a minister without one
a collection of an artist's work shown to clients

explanation.surface: A minister is put in charge of what an artist produces.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a cabinet minister's department and the case or collection of an artist's samples of work.

clue.text: Manages to get redesigned hive accepted by experts

indicators.note: accepted by says the reworked hive goes inside the experts

parts.note: aces are people who excel at something

indicators.note: redesigned says the letters of hive are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Beekeeping specialists approve a new hive design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redesigned' gives HIEV, which 'accepted by' tucks inside the experts; 'Manages to get' is the definition, not part of the mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve something is to succeed in obtaining or accomplishing it.

clue.text: An unexpected turn of events, and isn't he a litigant in a muddle?

indicators.note: in a muddle says these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A dramatic twist, and a confused courtroom claimant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a muddle' rearranges the fifteen letters of ISNTHEALITIGANT.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a nasty surprise coming at the very end of a story or situation.

clue.text: Devil with evidence of debts showing lack of respect

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
IOUs are written promises to pay, so proof of money owed

explanation.surface: A mischief-maker holding unpaid notes behaves disrespectfully.
explanation.walkthrough: IOU, 'I owe you', is a signed note of a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Impious means irreverent, lacking proper respect, especially toward religion.

clue.text: French wine circle entertaining old boy up for hot food

indicators.note: entertaining says the wine and circle play host, holding the old boy between them

parts.note: vin is French for wine
a circle has the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the old boy is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A French wine tasting circle hosts a former pupil for a spicy meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns OLAD into DALO; 'entertaining' sets it between VIN and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A vindaloo is a fiery curry, among the hottest dishes on an Indian restaurant menu.

clue.text: Brawn as speciality

definitions.meaning: a speciality is something one is especially good at, a forte

explanation.surface: Muscle power as one's particular talent.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means physical might and also a strong point, as in someone's main asset.

clue.text: Docked support vehicle at game

indicators.note: docked means cut short, so the support word loses its tail

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A support vehicle parked up at a boat dock, then a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Docked' removes the last letter of BACK, leaving BAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a card game played in casinos, betting against the banker.

clue.text: One's batting bottle is undone by this

definitions.meaning: in cricket, the batsman who starts an innings
a tool for taking caps off bottles

explanation.surface: A cricketer at the crease whose nerve fails him.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the first pair of batters in an innings are the openers. 'Bottle' in British slang is also nerve, which feeds the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an opening batter in cricket and a gadget for prising off caps.

clue.text: Aviators with female in agony must get fuel

indicators.note: in says the flyers and the woman go inside the word for agony

parts.note: agony is intense pain
the RAF is the Royal Air Force, Britain's flyers

explanation.surface: Pilots and a woman in distress must refuel.
explanation.walkthrough: RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin is kerosene, an oil burned in lamps, heaters and jet engines.

clue.text: Party chief's sphere of influence

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
main means chief or principal

explanation.surface: A party leader's area of control.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is a territory or field over which someone holds authority.

clue.text: Dogs eating last of dinner for miners

indicators.note: eating says the dogs take that letter inside them

parts.note: collies are sheepdogs

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of dinner

explanation.surface: Dogs finishing off the scraps of a meal meant for coal workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' gives R from dinner; 'eating' puts it inside COLLIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Colliers are coal miners, from colliery, a coal mine.

clue.text: Fancy ordering a barrier for some immigrants

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, so these letters are elaborated into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone imagines ordering a barrier to keep out immigrants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb meaning imagine but rearranges ORDERINGA.
explanation.definitionFit: The river forms much of the border between the US and Mexico, a natural obstacle that migrants cross.

clue.text: Yield from planned economy rejected

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Giving up on a state-controlled economy that has been turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' marks the hidden run, which 'rejected' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to give up or surrender, the verb sense of yield.

clue.text: Framed Frenchman after company acted

indicators.note: after says the Frenchman comes behind the company

parts.note: M is short for Monsieur, a French gentleman
posed means acted or put on a pretence

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is set up after a firm puts on an act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Framed' looks like set up for a crime but means put together, as a letter or song.
explanation.definitionFit: To frame a reply or a piece is to compose it, putting it together with care.

clue.text: Residence or fine home within the outskirts of Dorking

indicators.note: within says the fine and home pieces sit between those edge letters
the outskirts of picks the first and last letters of Dorking

parts.note: well means fine, in good health
in means at home

explanation.surface: A residence, or a nice house, on the edge of a Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the outskirts of' gives D and G from Dorking, a town in Surrey, England; 'within' puts WELLIN between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling is a house or other place where someone lives.

clue.text: Part of small hotel, originally upmarket

indicators.note: originally says take the opening letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: A small hotel that was once smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes initials from Part of small hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Posh means smart and expensive, appealing to the wealthy.

clue.text: Unusual prejudice seeing no judge initially offering treatment such as this

indicators.note: unusual says the remaining letters are put in an odd order
seeing no says that letter is removed from the word prejudice
initially picks the first letter of judge

explanation.surface: An odd bias that isn't seen in the first judge, offering treatment like this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeing no' with 'initially' removes J from PREJUDICE; 'Unusual' rearranges PREUDICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedicure is cosmetic care for the feet and toenails, a beauty treatment.

clue.text: American revolutionary with chewed cigar left such spirit

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning right round, so the American abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for American, as in US forces

indicators.note: chewed says the cigar is mangled, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A US rebel chewing a cigar leaves behind a kind of spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns US into SU; 'chewed' makes RGICA from CIGAR. 'such spirit' asks for the word that goes with spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgical spirit is the British name for rubbing alcohol, the antiseptic used to clean skin.

clue.text: Two ducks in New Forest getting tired

indicators.note: in says the ducks go inside the rearranged forest
new says the letters of forest are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so two are a pair of O shapes

explanation.surface: Walking among ducks in the New Forest leaves one weary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' gives FTSORE and 'in' holds the two ducks. The New Forest is a national park in southern England, so 'New' hides as part of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Footsore means having aching feet from walking, a particular kind of weariness.

clue.text: Delicate bit of cloth found in record cabinet

indicators.note: found in says the cloth scrap sits inside the cabinet

parts.note: a file is a cabinet or folder for records
a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: A delicate scrap of fabric turns up in a filing cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragile means easily broken or damaged, so needing delicate handling.

clue.text: Problem seen in Standard column

indicators.note: seen in says the trouble appears inside the standard

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
an ill is a trouble or misfortune

explanation.surface: A trouble spotted in a column of the Evening Standard newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on 'Standard' suggests the London newspaper, but it means PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar is an upright column supporting a building.

clue.text: Grannie's lost income from investments?

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters have gone astray and are found in a new order

explanation.surface: An old woman's savings have vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges GRANNIES; the question mark admits investments are only one source.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings are money received, whether wages or returns such as dividends.

clue.text: Short temper?

definitions.meaning: a short is a small measure of strong alcohol such as whisky
temper as mood or disposition, the mettle of a person

explanation.surface: A query about someone quick to anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like an adjective in short-tempered, but is a noun for a measure of hard liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a strong drink like gin and a person's mettle or mood.

clue.text: A woman of the cloth accepts no church state

indicators.note: accepts says the nun takes the word no inside her

parts.note: a nun is a female member of a religious order
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A nun takes in refusals from the church about the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a country but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something is to declare or proclaim it formally.

clue.text: Marine bank anticipating the Spanish nonsense

indicators.note: anticipating says the bank comes before the Spanish article

parts.note: Dogger Bank is a large sandbank in the North Sea, also a shipping forecast area
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A sea bank coming before the Spanish produces rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Dogger is one of the British radio shipping forecast's sea areas.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel is clumsy, trivial verse, so by extension worthless rubbish.

clue.text: The First Lady, 50, seen in New York regularly

parts.note: in the Bible Eve is the first woman

indicators.note: seen in says the fifty appears inside New York

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A US president's wife turning fifty is spotted in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The First Lady' suggests a president's wife but means the first woman in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Evenly means uniformly or at an even rate, in a steady regular way.
